```text
CoinCync 1.0 full node daemon

Usage: coincync-node.exe [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  start               Start the node (default if no command is given)
  print-genesis-hash  Print the genesis block hash and exit
  status              Show node status
  check-update        Check the GitHub releases page for a newer version and exit
  migrate-legacy-db   One-shot: stamp a pre-v1 chaindata as `schema_version = 1`, after validating the genesis block in the DB matches the expected genesis hash for `--network`. Operator-only escape hatch for upgrading from v1.0.11.x (no stamp) to v1.0.12+ (requires stamp)
  snapshot-export     Export a consistent chain snapshot for trusted fast-sync bootstrap
  snapshot-import     Install a chain snapshot produced by `snapshot-export`
  rollback            Roll a STOPPED node back to a given height, disconnecting every block above it and rebuilding supply/UTXO/work state down to that height. The rest of the data dir is kept
  help                Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --data-dir <DATA_DIR>
          Data directory
          
          [default: ~/.coincync]

      --network <NETWORK>
          Network
          
          [default: testnet]
          [possible values: mainnet, testnet, regtest, beta]

      --log-level <LOG_LEVEL>
          Log level
          
          [default: info]

      --p2p-bind <P2P_BIND>
          P2P listen address (overrides the network default)

      --max-connections-per-ip <MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_IP>
          Maximum simultaneous inbound connections accepted from a single IP (#193). Default 2. Raise this on a seed when several legitimate nodes share one public IP (a LAN behind one NAT); raising it weakens per-IP Sybil resistance, so set it only on hosts you control and trust the clients of
          
          [default: 2]

      --rpc-bind <RPC_BIND>
          RPC listen address (overrides the network default)

      --addnode <ADDNODE>
          Extra peer address(es) to try on startup

      --external-ip <IP[:PORT]>
          Our own externally-reachable address. Accepts a bare IP (`45.32.79.234`, our listen port is attached) or `IP:PORT`. Registered as a self-address so peer gossip that echoes our own IP back to us never makes us dial ourselves. Strongly recommended for fixed-IP fleet nodes

      --no-peers
          Disable all automatic peer discovery (for isolated tests)

      --proxy <HOST:PORT>
          SOCKS5 proxy address (e.g. `127.0.0.1:9050` for a local Tor daemon). When set, P2P connections AND DNS-seed queries route through the proxy. DNS uses DNS-over-TCP via the proxy (default resolver `1.1.1.1:53`; override with `COINCYNC_SOCKS_DNS_RESOLVER`) so the OS resolver never sees the seed hostnames

      --tor
          Convenience shortcut for `--proxy 127.0.0.1:9050` — the default Tor SOCKS5 listener. Ignored if `--proxy` is also set

      --onion-only
          Refuse to connect to clearnet peers — only `.onion` addresses accepted. Implies a proxy (`--tor` is added automatically if neither `--proxy` nor `--tor` is set). Use this when you require strict Tor-only operation; the node will reject any peer whose address isn't a `.onion` host

      --explorer
          Mount the embedded block explorer at GET / on the REST port.
          
          LOCAL DEVELOPMENT ONLY. For public deployment, run the standalone Caddy stack in `deploy/explorer/` instead — it isolates the explorer's public-facing HTTP from the consensus binary. See `deploy/explorer/README.md` for the full architectural rationale.

      --rest-bind <REST_BIND>
          Bind address for the REST + explorer server. Defaults to `127.0.0.1:<rpc_port + 2>`. Binding to a non-localhost address with `--explorer` set triggers a security warning at startup but is permitted

      --rest-disable
          Opt out of the REST layer entirely. By default the REST server is spawned on 127.0.0.1:<rpc_port + 2> on every node so that a load balancer (Cloudflare LB, nginx, HAProxy) fronting api.coincync.network can health-check every fleet host and route around a wedged one — closing the single-api-host SPOF that caused the 41-hour public-RPC outage on 2026-07-02.
          
          Set this flag on resource-constrained hosts that don't need the REST surface (e.g., miners running rig on the same box).

      --stratum <STRATUM>
          Enable the built-in Stratum mining-pool server on this bind address (e.g. `127.0.0.1:3333`). Off by default. Requires `--stratum-address` to actually produce blocks; a non-loopback bind is subject to the standard Stratum public-exposure policy (ACK + password + TLS/proxy)

      --stratum-address <STRATUM_ADDRESS>
          Payout address for the built-in Stratum pool — the coinbase of every block the pool finds is paid to a stealth address derived from this CYNC address. Required for the pool to build blocks

      --mine <MINE>
          SOLO MINE: run a built-in CPU miner in this same process, paying the coinbase to this CYNC address. One command = a node that mines to you, no separate `coincync-rig` needed. The node only ever sees the address's PUBLIC keys (no secret-key custody). Mines only when the node is synced, or on regtest, to avoid building a private fork. Mining with 0 peers is gated behind `--allow-solo-mine` (see below)

      --mine-threads <MINE_THREADS>
          Threads for the built-in solo miner (`--mine`). 0 = auto (CPU count)
          
          [default: 0]

      --allow-solo-mine
          Allow the built-in miner to mine with 0 peers on testnet/mainnet — for a designated BOOTSTRAP SEED only. OFF by default: a home node that loses peers (e.g. router outage) must NOT keep mining, or it builds a private fork it can't currently reorg off (issue #126). Regtest always mines

  -v, --verbose
          Verbose startup display. Prints the FULL consensus fingerprint (not the truncated form) and the configured bootstrap seed addresses in the startup banner. CAUTION: the seed list is network topology — only pass this when you are reading the output yourself, not piping it somewhere it could leak which peers this node reaches. The live IBD display always shows peer COUNT only, never addresses, regardless of this flag

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

### `coincync-node check-update`

```text
Check the GitHub releases page for a newer version and exit.

User-invoked only. The node does *not* poll for updates on startup — for a privacy coin, an automatic phone-home would leak "a CoinCync node is starting" from every user's IP to GitHub and intermediaries on every restart. Running this subcommand explicitly is informed-consent update checking.

Usage: coincync-node.exe check-update

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

### `coincync-node migrate-legacy-db`

```text
One-shot: stamp a pre-v1 chaindata as `schema_version = 1`, after validating the genesis block in the DB matches the expected genesis hash for `--network`. Operator-only escape hatch for upgrading from v1.0.11.x (no stamp) to v1.0.12+ (requires stamp).

Idempotent: re-running on an already-stamped DB is a no-op. Aborts if the DB belongs to a different chain (genesis hash mismatch). See `docs/operations/v1.0.12-hard-fork-rollout.md` for the full upgrade runbook.

Usage: coincync-node.exe migrate-legacy-db

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

### `coincync-node snapshot-export`

```text
Export a consistent chain snapshot for trusted fast-sync bootstrap.

The node MUST be stopped (the sled DB is single-process). Produces `<out>/db/` + `<out>/manifest.json`; copy that directory to a lagging node and run `snapshot-import` there instead of grinding IBD from genesis. See `src/snapshot.rs` for the format + trust model.

Usage: coincync-node.exe snapshot-export --out <OUT>

Options:
      --out <OUT>
          Output directory for the snapshot (must not already contain `db/`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

### `coincync-node snapshot-import`

```text
Install a chain snapshot produced by `snapshot-export`.

The node MUST be stopped. Verifies the snapshot's network + genesis hash (refuses a wrong-chain snapshot) and a blake3 integrity hash, backs up any existing chaindata to a `.pre-snapshot-<ts>` sibling (reversible), then installs the snapshot.

Usage: coincync-node.exe snapshot-import --input <INPUT>

Options:
      --input <INPUT>
          Snapshot directory (containing `db/` + `manifest.json`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

### `coincync-node rollback`

```text
Roll a STOPPED node back to a given height, disconnecting every block above it and rebuilding supply/UTXO/work state down to that height. The rest of the data dir is kept.

Recovery path for a node wedged on a private/minority fork (#286): a node that mined its own fork past the MESS floor can never reorg back to the real chain. Roll back to the last height it shares with the real chain, then restart — the node is now simply *behind*, not forked, and syncs forward normally. Refuses to cross a consensus checkpoint (finality is enforced). Block bodies above the target stay in the DB but are no longer canonical (a later resync overwrites the height index).

The node MUST be stopped (the DB is single-process; a running daemon holds the lock and this command refuses to open it). Prints the plan and exits WITHOUT changing anything unless `--yes` is given.

Usage: coincync-node.exe rollback [OPTIONS] --to-height <TO_HEIGHT>

Options:
      --to-height <TO_HEIGHT>
          Height to roll back to. Must be below the current tip and at or above the last checkpoint

      --yes
          Actually perform the rollback. Without this flag the command only reports what it would do (a dry run)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `coincync-wallet`

```text
CoinCync 1.0 wallet CLI

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  create              Create a new wallet with a fresh seed phrase
  restore             Restore a wallet from a 24-word seed phrase
  open                Open an existing wallet (just checks the password)
  info                Show wallet status + chain info from the node
  address             Show the spend public key (receive pubkey for this wallet)
  address-info        Decode a CoinCync address string into its spend/view public keys. Stateless — no wallet required. The GUI uses this to resolve a recipient address to raw pubkeys before `send`
  balance             Show balance snapshot from the wallet file (does NOT resync)
  integrated-address  Generate an integrated address: this wallet's address plus an 8-byte payment ID, so a sender's payment can be associated with an account / invoice. Share the printed address; the payment ID is recovered (encrypted) when the payment is received
  utxos               List the wallet's unspent outputs (amount, height, subaddress, spent). Reads the persisted UTXO sidecar — run `scan` first to populate it
  show-seed           Print the master seed as hex (requires password)
  scan                Scan blocks from the node for owned outputs
  privacy-stats       Show the current shielded-pool / Spark / MW stats from the node
  shielded-address    Print this wallet's shielded (Spark) receive address
  shielded-send       Build + verify a shielded (Spark) transfer to another wallet
  shielded-mint       Shield transparent funds INTO the Spark pool (a shield-in mint)
  shielded-unshield   Unshield pool value back to this wallet's TRANSPARENT balance: spend an owned shielded note, pay `amount` OUT of the pool as a value-revealing transparent output (public amount, to this wallet), and return the pool remainder as shielded change. The mirror of `shielded-mint`. Same gating
  shielded-balance    Show this wallet's shielded (Spark) balance from the node's cover set
  shielded-view-key   Export this wallet's WATCH-ONLY shielded view key as `<s1hex>:<p2hex>`
  send                Build and submit a privacy transaction to the node
  multisig-gen        Generate M-of-N multi-sig key shares using FROST
  multisig-info       Show multi-sig key share info
  multisig-round1     Multi-sig Round 1: generate nonces + commitments
  multisig-round2     Multi-sig Round 2: produce signature share
  multisig-send       Multi-sig Send: build + submit a privacy transaction using threshold key shares. Reconstructs the group key from M shares, signs CLSAG, submits, then zeroizes
  set-recovery        Set a dead man's switch recovery address for future transactions. If this wallet doesn't sign for --timeout blocks, the recovery address can sweep
  check-recovery      Check if any UTXOs have recovery metadata and their recovery status
  auto-churn          Enable auto-churn: automatic self-sends at random intervals to poison the transaction graph. Runs as a background loop until stopped
  multisig-aggregate  Multi-sig Aggregate: combine signature shares into final signature
  subaddress          Subaddress operations: list and generate unlinkable receiving addresses derived from this wallet's view+spend keys. Each subaddress is a distinct (account, index) tuple. Senders to different subaddresses cannot tell that they're paying the same wallet — the spend pubkeys are independent on chain even though they share a view key for scan
  disclose            Selective-disclosure proofs. Prove statements about owned UTXOs to a third party (auditor, KYC counterparty) without revealing values or one-time secrets. All non-interactive — proof bytes travel over any channel
  show-memo           Decrypt and print the encrypted memo attached to one of this wallet's UTXOs. Senders embed memos in the first recipient output via `send --memo`; the bytes are encrypted to the recipient's view key and round-trip through chain untouched. Only the recipient (this wallet) can read them
  treasury            Treasury protection: watch-only monitoring (and, later, spending policy)
  help                Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --wallet <WALLET>        Wallet file path [default: ~/.coincync/wallets/default.wallet]
      --network <NETWORK>      Network. `beta` is the public disposable test net where gated, unaudited features (e.g. the shielded pool) activate early; it mirrors testnet's address format, so beta wallets and testnet wallets are interchangeable [default: testnet] [possible values: mainnet, testnet, regtest, beta]
      --node <NODE>            Node RPC URL [default: http://127.0.0.1:28081]
      --log-level <LOG_LEVEL>  Log level [default: warn]
  -h, --help                   Print help
  -V, --version                Print version
```

### `coincync-wallet shielded-send`

```text
Build + verify a shielded (Spark) transfer to another wallet.

EXPERIMENTAL / regtest-only: shielded txs are activation-gated OFF on testnet/mainnet and there is no shielded node RPC yet, so this runs the full transfer path end to end against a local regtest pool (funds this wallet, scans, builds, and NODE-verifies a real shielded transfer) and reports it. Live submission awaits activation + a shielded RPC. Present only in a `sketch-gk-proof + libspark-ffi` build.

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe shielded-send [OPTIONS] --to <TO> --amount <AMOUNT>

Options:
      --to <TO>
          Recipient's bech32m Spark address (see `shielded-address`)

      --amount <AMOUNT>
          Amount to send, in atomic units

      --demo
          Self-contained REGTEST run: bootstrap a local pool, fund this wallet, then build + verify — no node needed. Without this the command fetches the live node's cover set via `get_shielded_cover_set` (`--node`) and builds against it

  -p, --password <PASSWORD>
          Wallet password. Use `-` to read from stdin. Reads `COINCYNC_WALLET_PASSWORD` env if neither flag nor stdin is provided
          
          [env: COINCYNC_WALLET_PASSWORD]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

### `coincync-wallet shielded-mint`

```text
Shield transparent funds INTO the Spark pool (a shield-in mint).

Spends this wallet's transparent UTXOs to create `amount` atomic units of SHIELDED value owned by this wallet (a real transparent-funded shield-in: ring-signed transparent inputs + an authenticated mint bundle + `value_balance = −amount`), then submits the `TxType::Shielded` tx via `send_raw_transaction`. EXPERIMENTAL: pre-activation the node accepts it structurally but it will not CONFIRM until shielded activation (`SHIELDED_TX_ACTIVATION_HEIGHT`). Requires a synced wallet (`wallet scan`) and `--node`. Present only in a `sketch-gk-proof + libspark-ffi` build.

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe shielded-mint [OPTIONS] --amount <AMOUNT>

Options:
      --amount <AMOUNT>
          Amount to shield in, in atomic units

  -p, --password <PASSWORD>
          Wallet password. Use `-` to read from stdin. Reads `COINCYNC_WALLET_PASSWORD` env if neither flag nor stdin is provided
          
          [env: COINCYNC_WALLET_PASSWORD]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

### `coincync-wallet shielded-view-key`

```text
Export this wallet's WATCH-ONLY shielded view key as `<s1hex>:<p2hex>`.

The holder can scan/report shielded balance (`shielded-balance --view-key`) but CANNOT spend. EXPERIMENTAL / regtest-gated; present only in a `sketch-gk-proof + libspark-ffi` build.

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe shielded-view-key [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>
          Wallet password. Use `-` to read from stdin. Reads `COINCYNC_WALLET_PASSWORD` env if neither flag nor stdin is provided
          
          [env: COINCYNC_WALLET_PASSWORD]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

### `coincync-wallet send`

```text
Build and submit a privacy transaction to the node

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe send [OPTIONS] --amount <AMOUNT>

Options:
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>
          Wallet password. Use `-` to read from stdin (recommended for piped automation: `echo $pw | wallet ... --password -`). Reads `COINCYNC_WALLET_PASSWORD` env if neither flag nor stdin is provided; otherwise prompts interactively [env: COINCYNC_WALLET_PASSWORD]
      --address <ADDRESS>
          Recipient address string (standard, subaddress, or integrated). When given, its spend/view keys, address type, and any embedded payment ID are used directly, so --to-spend/--to-view/--payment-id/--subaddress are not needed. This is the way to pay an integrated address
      --to-spend <TO_SPEND>
          Recipient spend public key (64-hex). Not needed when --address is given
      --to-view <TO_VIEW>
          Recipient view public key (64-hex). Not needed when --address is given
      --amount <AMOUNT>
          Amount to send, in atomic CYNC units
      --fee-multiplier <FEE_MULTIPLIER>
          Fee multiplier (1.0 = normal, 2.0 = double fee for priority) [default: 1.0]
      --split-output
          Drip-pair: split the amount into 2 outputs to the same recipient (no change). Lets a first-time recipient receive 2 UTXOs in a single uniform 2-in/2-out tx so they can immediately spend (since spending also requires 2 UTXOs). Excess input value goes to fee — use this only when input UTXOs are sized close to the drip amount, otherwise you'll pay a large fee. Used by the testnet faucet's onboarding flow
      --subaddress
          Mark the recipient as a subaddress. Subaddress outputs use tx pubkey R = r*D_i so the recipient can detect/spend them against their published view key C_i = a*D_i. Set this ONLY when `--to-view` is a subaddress view key (C_i); a main-address send must leave it off (default). Sending to a subaddress WITHOUT this flag produces an output the recipient cannot detect or spend
      --memo <MEMO>
          Optional plaintext memo (max 256 bytes). Encrypted on the first recipient output using the recipient's view key — only the recipient can decrypt. Useful for human-readable notes ("rent june", "for coffee") or invoice IDs that don't belong on-chain in plaintext
      --recovery-address <RECOVERY_ADDRESS>
          Dead-man's switch — recovery address (64-hex spend pubkey of a backup wallet). If this wallet doesn't sign for `--recovery-timeout` blocks, the recovery wallet can sweep the outputs of this tx. Embeds a 42-byte RecoveryMeta into `tx.extra`. Both flags must be passed together
      --recovery-timeout <RECOVERY_TIMEOUT>
          Blocks of inactivity before recovery activates (min 720 ≈ 24h, max 525960 ≈ 2yr). Required when `--recovery-address` is set; ignored otherwise
      --payment-id <PAYMENT_ID>
          Integrated-address payment ID (16-hex / 8 bytes). Carried encrypted in tx.extra and recovered by the recipient on scan. Use when paying an exchange that issued you an integrated address
      --policy <POLICY>
          Treasury allowlist policy file (from `treasury allow`). When set, the send is REFUSED unless the recipient (spend+view) is on the list — a guard against a compromised host or operator redirecting funds. This is enforced by this wallet binary; pair it with M-of-N custody for protection a single compromised signer cannot bypass
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

### `coincync-wallet disclose`

```text
Selective-disclosure proofs. Prove statements about owned UTXOs to a third party (auditor, KYC counterparty) without revealing values or one-time secrets. All non-interactive — proof bytes travel over any channel

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe disclose <COMMAND>

Commands:
  balance               Prove a specific UTXO's amount is at least `--threshold` without revealing the actual amount. Useful for proof-of-funds at a counterparty without exposing balance
  verify-balance        Verify a hex-encoded balance proof. No wallet keys needed — anyone can verify
  verify-ownership      Verify a hex-encoded ownership proof. The wallet owner produces the OwnershipProof out-of-band; the auditor pastes the proof here
  scoped-view-key       Export a time-scoped view key: a read-only key that decrypts only outputs in blocks [--from-height, --to-height]. Discloses your history for a bounded period (e.g. a tax year) without giving up past-or-future privacy. Contains a view secret — share carefully
  scan-scoped           Auditor side: scan a scoped view key's block range and list the outputs it can see. Read-only, no wallet, bounded to the key's disclosed range
  verify-audit-package  Auditor side (stateless, no wallet): verify an org-signed audit package against a node. The org produces a signed package with the library (`PayrollRun` → `sign`); the auditor points this at their node, which checks the org signature and anchors every disclosure proof against real chain state, then returns the verdict, reconciliation, and a report
  build-payroll-audit   Org side: build and sign a payroll/settlement audit package for one named auditor. Proves treasury solvency from one of this wallet's UTXOs; optionally adds a total-disbursed proof (from a disbursements file the org holds, since only it knows those outputs' blindings) and recipient receipts (DisclosureProof JSON the recipients handed over). Signs with the org's Ed25519 audit key and writes a SignedAuditPackage the auditor verifies with `verify-audit-package`
  export-output         Recipient side: export one received output as a disbursement entry ({value, blinding, tx_hash, output_index}) for the payer's `build-payroll-audit --disbursements` file. Reveals this output's amount and blinding to the payer (who paid it), so share it only with them
  receipt               Recipient side: produce an ownership receipt (a DisclosureProof) for one received output, proving control of it without revealing the one-time key. Hand this to the payer for their audit package
  help                  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

#### `coincync-wallet disclose balance`

```text
Prove a specific UTXO's amount is at least `--threshold` without revealing the actual amount. Useful for proof-of-funds at a counterparty without exposing balance

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe disclose balance [OPTIONS] --threshold <THRESHOLD>

Options:
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>      Wallet password. Use `-` to read from stdin (recommended for piped automation: `echo $pw | wallet ... --password -`). Reads `COINCYNC_WALLET_PASSWORD` env if neither flag nor stdin is provided; otherwise prompts interactively [env: COINCYNC_WALLET_PASSWORD]
      --utxo <UTXO>              Stable selector for the UTXO: `TXID:VOUT`. Preferred — an outpoint does not shift as the chain grows and the wallet rescans. Give this OR `--utxo-index`
      --utxo-index <UTXO_INDEX>  Legacy positional index into the wallet's unspent list (0-based; fragile across rescans — prefer `--utxo`). Give this OR `--utxo`
      --threshold <THRESHOLD>    Threshold value in atomic units. Asserts `utxo.amount >= threshold`. Must be <= actual value
  -h, --help                     Print help
```

#### `coincync-wallet disclose verify-balance`

```text
Verify a hex-encoded balance proof. No wallet keys needed — anyone can verify.

Without `--anchor-tx`, this checks only the range-proof math over the prover-supplied commitment (NOT proof of on-chain funds). Pass `--anchor-tx <hash>` and `--anchor-output-index <n>` to also verify the commitment matches that real on-chain output (queried via `--node`).

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe disclose verify-balance [OPTIONS] --proof <PROOF>

Options:
      --proof <PROOF>
          

      --anchor-tx <ANCHOR_TX>
          On-chain tx hash (hex) whose output the proof should match. When set with `--anchor-output-index`, upgrades the check to chain-anchored

      --anchor-output-index <ANCHOR_OUTPUT_INDEX>
          Index of the output within `--anchor-tx` to anchor against

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

#### `coincync-wallet disclose verify-ownership`

```text
Verify a hex-encoded ownership proof. The wallet owner produces the OwnershipProof out-of-band; the auditor pastes the proof here.

Without `--anchor`, this checks only the Schnorr signature over the prover-declared (stealth_address, tx_hash, output_index) — NOT proof of real on-chain funds. Pass `--anchor` to also confirm the on-chain output at the proof's own (tx_hash, output_index) has that stealth address (queried via `--node`).

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe disclose verify-ownership [OPTIONS] --proof <PROOF>

Options:
      --proof <PROOF>
          

      --anchor
          Anchor the proof against the on-chain output at its declared (tx_hash, output_index), fetched from `--node`

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

#### `coincync-wallet disclose verify-audit-package`

```text
Auditor side (stateless, no wallet): verify an org-signed audit package against a node. The org produces a signed package with the library (`PayrollRun` → `sign`); the auditor points this at their node, which checks the org signature and anchors every disclosure proof against real chain state, then returns the verdict, reconciliation, and a report

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe disclose verify-audit-package --package <PACKAGE> --issuer <ISSUER> --auditor <AUDITOR>

Options:
      --package <PACKAGE>  Path to the SignedAuditPackage JSON file
      --issuer <ISSUER>    Ed25519 public key (hex, 32 bytes) the auditor expects the issuing org to have signed with — known out of band, never from the package
      --auditor <AUDITOR>  The auditor identity this package must be addressed to (its `audience`); a package issued to anyone else is rejected
  -h, --help               Print help
```

#### `coincync-wallet disclose build-payroll-audit`

```text
Org side: build and sign a payroll/settlement audit package for one named auditor. Proves treasury solvency from one of this wallet's UTXOs; optionally adds a total-disbursed proof (from a disbursements file the org holds, since only it knows those outputs' blindings) and recipient receipts (DisclosureProof JSON the recipients handed over). Signs with the org's Ed25519 audit key and writes a SignedAuditPackage the auditor verifies with `verify-audit-package`

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe disclose build-payroll-audit [OPTIONS] --org <ORG> --period <PERIOD> --threshold <THRESHOLD> --auditor <AUDITOR> --out <OUT>

Options:
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>
          [env: COINCYNC_WALLET_PASSWORD]
      --org <ORG>
          Organization name recorded in the package
      --period <PERIOD>
          Period label (e.g. "2026-Q3")
      --treasury-utxo <TREASURY_UTXO>
          Stable selector for the treasury UTXO: `TXID:VOUT`. Preferred over `--treasury-utxo-index` because an outpoint does not shift as the chain grows and the wallet rescans. With `--treasury-count K > 1`, this names the FIRST of the K outputs (the rest follow it in the unspent list). Give this OR `--treasury-utxo-index`
      --treasury-utxo-index <TREASURY_UTXO_INDEX>
          Legacy positional index of the treasury UTXO in the wallet's unspent list (run `scan` first). Fragile across rescans — prefer `--treasury-utxo TXID:VOUT`. Give this OR `--treasury-utxo`
      --threshold <THRESHOLD>
          Solvency threshold in atomic units (asserts treasury >= threshold)
      --signing-seed <SIGNING_SEED>
          The org's Ed25519 audit signing seed (hex, 32 bytes). Distinct from wallet keys — it is the org's audit identity. Reads `COINCYNC_AUDIT_SIGNING_SEED` if the flag is omitted [env: COINCYNC_AUDIT_SIGNING_SEED]
      --auditor <AUDITOR>
          The single auditor this package is addressed to (its `audience`)
      --audit-id <AUDIT_ID>
          Unique single-use id (hex, 32 bytes). Random if omitted
      --expires-at <EXPIRES_AT>
          Package expiry as a unix timestamp (seconds). Never expires if unset
      --disbursements <DISBURSEMENTS>
          Optional disbursements JSON file adding a total-disbursed proof: {"height_range":[start,end],"outputs":[{"value":u64, "blinding":"hex32","tx_hash":"hex32","output_index":u8}, …]}
      --receipt <RECEIPTS>
          Recipient receipt file (a DisclosureProof JSON). Repeatable
      --unlinkable-solvency
          Prove treasury solvency WITHOUT revealing which output is the treasury: hide it among `--anon-size` real on-chain outputs (a Groth-Kohlweiss one-of-many). Replaces the linkable balance proof
      --anon-size <ANON_SIZE>
          Anonymity-set size for `--unlinkable-solvency` (power of two >= 2) [default: 8]
      --treasury-count <TREASURY_COUNT>
          Number of treasury outputs to prove over (K). With `K > 1`, proves the SUM of K hidden outputs `>= threshold`, each hidden in its own disjoint set (multi-output unlinkable solvency). Uses wallet UTXOs `[treasury-utxo-index .. +K]`. Default 1 [default: 1]
      --out <OUT>
          Output path for the signed package JSON
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

### `coincync-wallet treasury`

```text
Treasury protection: watch-only monitoring (and, later, spending policy)

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe treasury <COMMAND>

Commands:
  watchfile  Export a watch file for a monitor: each treasury output's key image plus its ref and amount. Contains NO spending secrets — a key image cannot spend, only reveal that an output moved — so it is safe to place on a separate, less-trusted monitoring box
  watch      Watch-only: poll the node (`--node`) for any spent treasury output and raise an alert. Needs only the watch file — no wallet, no keys. Exits non-zero if any watched output has moved, so it can drive cron/alerting
  allow      Add an approved recipient to a treasury allowlist policy file (created if missing). `send --policy <file>` then refuses any recipient not listed
  velocity   Set a per-window outflow cap in a policy file. `send --policy <file>` then refuses a send whose amount, plus everything already sent in the trailing window, would exceed the cap. A compromised signer still can't drain fast
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

#### `coincync-wallet treasury watchfile`

```text
Export a watch file for a monitor: each treasury output's key image plus its ref and amount. Contains NO spending secrets — a key image cannot spend, only reveal that an output moved — so it is safe to place on a separate, less-trusted monitoring box

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe treasury watchfile [OPTIONS] --out <OUT>

Options:
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  [env: COINCYNC_WALLET_PASSWORD]
      --out <OUT>            Output path for the watch file (JSON)
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

#### `coincync-wallet treasury watch`

```text
Watch-only: poll the node (`--node`) for any spent treasury output and raise an alert. Needs only the watch file — no wallet, no keys. Exits non-zero if any watched output has moved, so it can drive cron/alerting

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe treasury watch --watchfile <WATCHFILE>

Options:
      --watchfile <WATCHFILE>  Path to the watch file from `treasury watchfile`
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

#### `coincync-wallet treasury allow`

```text
Add an approved recipient to a treasury allowlist policy file (created if missing). `send --policy <file>` then refuses any recipient not listed

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe treasury allow [OPTIONS] --spend <SPEND> --view <VIEW> --policy <POLICY>

Options:
      --spend <SPEND>    Recipient spend public key (64-hex)
      --view <VIEW>      Recipient view public key (64-hex)
      --label <LABEL>    Optional human label (e.g. "payroll:bob")
      --policy <POLICY>  Policy file to create/append
  -h, --help             Print help
```

#### `coincync-wallet treasury velocity`

```text
Set a per-window outflow cap in a policy file. `send --policy <file>` then refuses a send whose amount, plus everything already sent in the trailing window, would exceed the cap. A compromised signer still can't drain fast

Usage: coincync-wallet.exe treasury velocity --max-atomic <MAX_ATOMIC> --window-secs <WINDOW_SECS> --policy <POLICY>

Options:
      --max-atomic <MAX_ATOMIC>    Maximum total outflow per window, in atomic CYNC units
      --window-secs <WINDOW_SECS>  Rolling window length in seconds (e.g. 86400 = 24h)
      --policy <POLICY>            Policy file to create/update
  -h, --help                       Print help
```

---

## Cargo / build command surface

The gated feature set is read live from `.github/workflows/shielded-gate.yml` so it always matches CI:

```text
GATED_FEATURES = testnet fuse block-integrity-breaker supply-breaker shielded-breaker regtest-chaos sketch-gk-proof libspark-ffi
```

### Canonical recipes

```bash
# Standard release build (ring-privacy chain, shielded OFF)
cargo build --release --features "randomx testnet"

# Gated CORRECTNESS suite — the 2400/0 bar. NEVER with test-fast-pow.
SPARK_OPENSSL_DIR=/usr COINCYNC_RANDOMX_LIGHT_MODE=1 \
  cargo test --release --lib --features "testnet fuse block-integrity-breaker supply-breaker shielded-breaker regtest-chaos sketch-gk-proof libspark-ffi"

# Gated integration + lock-integrity check (what CI runs)
cargo test  --release --features "testnet fuse block-integrity-breaker supply-breaker shielded-breaker regtest-chaos sketch-gk-proof libspark-ffi" --test full_pipeline_real_crypto
cargo check --release --features "testnet fuse block-integrity-breaker supply-breaker shielded-breaker regtest-chaos sketch-gk-proof libspark-ffi"        # runs build.rs lock guard

# Chaos HARNESS binaries — WITH test-fast-pow (instant mining). Harness only,
# never a correctness build (test-fast-pow skips real PoW).
cargo build --release --features "randomx testnet fuse block-integrity-breaker supply-breaker shielded-breaker regtest-chaos sketch-gk-proof libspark-ffi test-fast-pow" --bin coincync-node --bin coincync-wallet

# Regenerate critical_files.lock after a reviewed change to a locked file
COINCYNC_REGEN_LOCK=1 cargo run --locked --release --bin update-critical-hashes

# Per-crate (rig miner shown; swap -p for any crate below)
cargo build --release -p coincync-rig

# Regenerate THIS doc
scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh            # dump prebuilt binaries
scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh --build    # build gated binaries first (NOT during a soak)
```

> Windows/WSL build env (clang + static OpenSSL for libspark) is documented in
> [`DEVELOPER.md`](DEVELOPER.md) — `LIBCLANG_PATH`, `SPARK_OPENSSL_DIR`,
> `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, `RUST_MIN_STACK`.

### Buildable targets

- `coincync-node`, `coincync-wallet` (root package bins)
- root helper bins: `bootstrap_manifest_tool`, `coincync-tick`, `diag`, `release_attest`, `sign_snapshot`, `stratum_ban_tool`, `update_critical_hashes`
- workspace crates (`-p <name>`): `auxpow`, `bridge`, `coincync-dbg`, `coincync-faucet`, `coincync-frost-coordinator`, `coincync-rig`, `coincync-rolling-finality`, `coincync-swap`, `cynchub`, `cytop`, `orchard-side`, `spark-connector`, `tick`
